models.name: Neural Network (MLP)
models.desc: Two hidden layers (64, 32) with ReLU and early stopping.

models.name: SVM (RBF)
models.desc: Non-linear margin classifier using an RBF kernel (fit on up to 6,000 rows for speed).

models.name: Logistic Regression
models.desc: Linear baseline: log-odds of churn as a weighted sum of features.

models.name: Linear Discriminant
models.desc: Finds the linear boundary that best separates churners from stayers (Gaussian classes).

models.name: K-Nearest Neighbors
models.desc: Votes among the 25 most similar customers.

models.name: Naive Bayes
models.desc: Bayes rule with independent Gaussian features. Fast and surprisingly strong.

cls_formulas.name: Accuracy
cls_formulas.note: Share of all predictions that are correct.

cls_formulas.name: Precision
cls_formulas.note: Of customers flagged as churners, how many really churned.

cls_formulas.name: Recall (Sensitivity)
cls_formulas.note: Of real churners, how many we caught.

cls_formulas.name: Specificity
cls_formulas.note: Of real stayers, how many we correctly left alone.

cls_formulas.name: F1 Score
cls_formulas.note: Harmonic mean of precision and recall.

cls_formulas.name: Balanced Accuracy
cls_formulas.note: Accuracy that is fair under class imbalance.

cls_formulas.name: Matthews Corr. Coef.
cls_formulas.formula: (TP x TN - FP x FN) / sqrt((TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN))
cls_formulas.note: -1 to +1 correlation between prediction and truth.

cls_formulas.name: PR-AUC
cls_formulas.formula: Area under the Precision-vs-Recall curve (average precision)
cls_formulas.note: Useful when churners are the minority.

cls_formulas.name: Brier Score
cls_formulas.note: Mean squared error of the probabilities.

ts_formulas.name: MAE
ts_formulas.note: Average absolute error, in churn-rate units.

ts_formulas.name: RMSE
ts_formulas.note: Like MAE but punishes big misses more.

ts_formulas.name: R-squared
ts_formulas.note: Below 0 means worse than predicting the mean.

forecast.note: No date column found, so rows (ordered by customer_id) are grouped into 60 equal acquisition cohorts; each cohort is treated as one period.
